content.text:
This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor.

The image has pixel rulers along its top and left edges (x increases to the right, y increases downward, 0 at the image's top-left corner). Using the ruler scale, give the position of a point inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: (x, y)

This axial slice shows a limb cross-section with two bones (the dark rings with marrow at about (362, 395) and (390, 540)). The large soft-tissue mass fills most of the limb. A fibrous tumor appears as a fairly homogeneous intermediate-signal region. The area to the right of the bones, around x 380–550 and y 300–560, looks homogeneous and is the likely tumor.

The left lower region, around (300, 450), has a different texture with a darker, heterogeneous area, so it is probably muscle. The tumor center is therefore estimated at about (450, 440).

ANSWER: (450, 440)
